title: Non-Religious Americans Just Passed Catholics
source: Pew Research Center's religious-identity trend surveys: the religiously unaffiliated ("nones") share of US adults rose from 16% (2007) to 17% (2009), 22.8% (2014, Religious Landscape Study), 26% (2019), and 29% (2021 NPORS) — overtaking Catholics, who declined from 24% (2007) to 23% (2009), roughly 21% (2014, 2019, 2021) and 19% (2023-24 Religious Landscape Study, published Feb 2025). Pew's newest study confirms the unaffiliated are now the single largest religious-identity group in America.
